newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks squeak ahead despite losses in golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks squeak ahead despite losses in golds.

text.p: Strength in forest products helped Toronto stocks to close higher on Friday despite havoc in the powerful gold sector.
The Toronto Stock Exchange Composite 300 Index closed at 5919.49, up 15.18 points. A total of 60.33 million shares worth C$893.83 million (US$652.23 million) traded hands.
Advancers outnumbered decliners 501 to 399, with 257 unchanged.
"I guess we would have done better were it not for a slight market crash in the area of golds," said Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president at ScotiaMcLeod in Toronto.
Comex February gold fell to new three-year lows, losing US$4.60 to close at US$362.00 an ounce. The steep drop pummeled Toronto's golds, with the gold subindex down 2.16 percent.

Barrick Gold Corp. lost C$1 down to C$37.60 and Placer Dome Inc. dropped C$0.75 to C$28.50. Gold royalty company Euro-Nevada Mining Corp. Ltd. lost almost five percent of its value, down C$1.90 to C$38.
The paper and forest products subindex gained 2.03 percent on Friday with investors betting on higher commodity prices in the future, Ketchen said.
Avenor Inc. gained C$0.55 to C$21.10 and Domtar Inc. rose C$0.60 to C$12.20.
High-tech stocks also made steady gains on Friday, borrowing strength from the U.S. markets, traders said.
Imperial Oil Ltd. sank C$2.45 to C$62 after the Toronto Stock Exchange said it removed the company from its Toronto 35 index of stocks.
Potash Corp. rose C$2.35 to C$117.25 after a U.S. judge dismissed an antitrust lawsuit accusing major Canadian and U.S. potash producers of price fixing.
